I don't have file-write access in this session, so here's the handoff note as text for you to drop into wherever your team keeps these (repo README, wiki, ticket, etc.) — likely a `HANDOFF.md` on the `oauth-migration` branch.

---

## OAuth2 Migration Handoff — Billing Service

**Owner (out):** [your name] — back [date one week from 2026-08-04]
**Owner (in):** [teammate name] — new to this project
**Branch:** `oauth-migration`

### Last completed action
Auth middleware and token-refresh logic have been rewritten for OAuth2 and merged into `oauth-migration`. Unit tests pass for both. Nothing beyond this has been done — no downstream services touched, no production config touched, no key rotation.

### Changed conditions (things not true before this work started)
- The billing service itself can now issue/validate OAuth2 tokens, but it still also accepts the old API-key auth path — this is intentional, not leftover.
- Old API keys are **still live and must stay live**. Do not deactivate, rotate, or expire any old API keys until all three downstream services below are confirmed migrated. If the keys go away first, those services will start getting 401s in production.

### Remaining scope (not yet started)
1. Migrate the three downstream services that currently call the old auth endpoints to use OAuth2 instead. [Name them here if you have exact service names — I don't have that detail.]
2. Update production config for the new auth flow.
3. Only after (1) and (2) are done and verified: rotate/retire the old API keys.

### Authority limits
- [Teammate] should not rotate or deactivate any API keys under any circumstances without confirming all three downstream services are migrated and verified in production — not just merged, actually verified working.
- [Teammate] should not touch production config until the downstream service migrations are done, since config changes here likely control which auth path is live.
- If anything here is ambiguous or the downstream services turn out to be more/less coupled than described, stop and check with [you / team lead / on-call] rather than guessing.

### Open evidence / what's unverified
- Only unit tests have been run on the middleware and token-refresh code — no integration testing against the downstream services has happened yet, since they haven't been migrated.
- I have not confirmed whether the three downstream services have any other dependencies on the old auth endpoints beyond what's currently known.

### Stop conditions
- Do not rotate old API keys until all three downstream services are migrated **and verified**.
- Do not deploy production config changes until downstream migrations are complete.
- If a downstream service migration surfaces unexpected auth behavior, pause and escalate rather than pushing forward.

### Before starting, [teammate] should confirm back
- Their understanding of the remaining scope (the three downstream migrations + config + key rotation, in that order).
- That they will not rotate keys or touch prod config until downstream services are done.
- Who to contact if something is unclear or breaks while you're out.

---

Fill in: the three downstream service names, links to the PRs/branch, ticket number, and an escalation contact for while you're away. Want me to also draft a shorter Slack-message version for a quick async ping to your team lead?
